reason: The hypothesis relies on general principles of entropy and atomic mismatch (E1) and on W benefits in Fe-based amorphous alloys (E2), but neither passage provides direct evidence for W addition in the specific high-entropy CrMnFeCoNi-P system; the extrapolation from Fe-based to this multi-principal-element alloy is unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: High configurational entropy favors amorphous formation over crystalline phases
Atomic size mismatch and bonding heterogeneity disrupt crystal nucleation and slow grain growth
Addition of high-melting-point, large-atom metals (e.g., W) can improve glass-forming ability and thermal stability in Fe-based amorphous alloys
